clue.text: Old sailor's side of pig in fat

indicators.note: in places the word for the animal inside the word for the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A side of pork wrapped in lard, perhaps from an old ship's galley.
explanation.walkthrough: LARBOARD is the old word for the port side of a ship, replaced because it was too easily confused with starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Old seafaring term for the port, left-hand side of a vessel.

clue.text: Vessel for cooling hands in shanty

definitions.text: Vessel for cooling hands in shanty

parts.words: Vessel for cooling hands in shanty
parts.note: the sea shanty about the drunken sailor proposes putting him in a ship's small rowing boat till he's sober, so drunk crewmen (hands) are cooled off there

explanation.surface: A container for cooling one's hands inside a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanty' looks like a shack, but it is a sailors' work song: 'What shall we do with the drunken sailor?' answers 'Put him in the long boat till he's sober'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large rowing boat carried aboard a sailing ship, a vessel of a kind.

clue.text: Transcribe copy of Echo or Mirror

definitions.meaning: to transcribe is to copy out or duplicate
an echo copies a sound and a mirror copies an image; Echo and Mirror are also newspaper names

explanation.surface: Writing out a copy of an article from the Echo or the Mirror newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean make a duplicate, whether in writing or as sound and image do.

clue.text: Drunk cooked, omitting a starter

indicators.note: dropping the starter means the first letter of the cooked word goes

parts.note: boiled is a way of having cooked something

explanation.surface: Someone cooked a meal while drunk and forgot to make a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, but here it is the first letter, B, removed from BOILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated, as if well lubricated with drink.

clue.text: Drunk after wine, as Ruby is sometimes

indicators.note: after places the word for drunk behind the wine in the answer

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
cut is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone called Ruby gets drunk after drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruby' looks like a woman's name, but it is the gemstone, which may be cut with a flat base and triangular facets. CUT for drunk is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem style with a flat base and faceted dome, used for rubies and diamonds.

clue.text: Tack the least worn?

definitions.meaning: to tack is to sew loosely with long temporary ...
not wearing a ... means wearing nothing at all, so this is the least clothing one could have on

explanation.definitionFit: Tacking means sewing a quick loop with needle and thread, and 'not a stitch on' means naked.

clue.text: Right about entrance to cutting

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for right is turned round

parts.note: to entrance (stress on the second syllable) is to enchant or bewitch

explanation.surface: A rite performed around the entrance to a railway cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway but is the verb meaning to bewitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are sharp and incisive, as cutting remarks are.

clue.text: Short kind of shirt (Gaelic)

parts.note: a T-shirt is a kind of shirt, giving the letter T
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A description of a short shirt in Gaelic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and curt.

clue.text: Hearts — card-game for three (or one in Spain)

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card notation
ombre is an old card game for three players

explanation.surface: A note on the card game Hearts and a three-handed game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts' looks like another card game, but supplies only H. HOMBRE is Spanish for man.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for a man, so a person or fellow there.

clue.text: St Paul's site yields bones

definitions.meaning: the apostle Paul was born in a city in Cilicia, now southern Turkey
the group of small bones of the ankle and upper foot

explanation.surface: The place connected with St Paul produces archaeological bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's birthplace city shares its name with the anatomical ankle bones.

clue.text: Tyneside butty for the high country

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
butty is northern and Welsh dialect for a mate or pal

explanation.surface: A Geordie sandwich (butty) taken to the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butty' suggests a sandwich, but in northern English and Welsh dialect it also means a workmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan kingdom, home to Everest, so a lofty land.

clue.text: "Tin", a Grand National favourite, is beaten

definitions.text: "Tin", a Grand National favourite, is beaten

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Red Rum was the horse who won the Grand National steeplechase three times

explanation.surface: A racehorse called Tin, a Grand National favourite, loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase. The whole clue also defines: a drum, as tins can be, gets beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum with rattling wires across its underside, which is struck with sticks.

clue.text: American sticks present cuts

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
to dock is to cut short, as a tail

explanation.surface: An American gift of sticks that have been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' is not wood but the American idiom for remote backwoods country.
explanation.definitionFit: US slang for remote rural backwoods, also called the sticks.

clue.text: Comfort for so long, leaving No 10

indicators.note: leaving means the letters for number ten depart from the farewell word

parts.note: cheerio is a British goodbye, 'so long'
IO looks like the number 10

explanation.surface: A politician seeks comfort after a long stay, leaving Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' suggests 10 Downing Street, but it is the number written as IO.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to gladden or hearten them.

clue.text: This Scandinavian spirit has water in opposition to it

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water
V for versus, as in a match, means in opposition to

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian liquor that refuses to be mixed with water.
explanation.definitionFit: A caraway-flavoured spirit from Scandinavia.

clue.text: All I crave-treatment for these spots

indicators.note: giving these words a treatment works them over into a new order

explanation.surface: A child with spots longs for any treatment at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment' looks medical, which suits the spots, but signals rearranging ALL I CRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical name for chickenpox, a disease known for its itchy spots.

clue.text: Becky's family, tone-raising characters

definitions.meaning: Becky Sharp is the scheming heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair
symbols in music that raise a note by a semitone

explanation.surface: Becky's relatives are characters who make things classier.
explanation.definitionFit: Becky Sharp's kin share her surname, and musical sharp signs raise a note.

clue.text: He preaches in a knotted purple tie!

indicators.note: knotted suggests the letters of these two words tied up into a new order

explanation.surface: A preacher in the pulpit wears a knotted purple tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory word for a preacher who holds forth from the pulpit.

clue.text: Place to stop for a beer, say, before going to church

definitions.text: Place to stop for a beer, say, before going to church

parts.words: Place to stop for a beer, say, before going to church
parts.note: a roofed churchyard entrance where a coffin rests on its bier, a homophone of beer, before the funeral service

explanation.surface: A pub stop on the way to church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub, but a bier carries a coffin, which once paused under the roofed churchyard gateway.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed gateway to a churchyard where a coffin waited for the clergy.

clue.text: Confused brides refuse

indicators.note: confused suggests the letters of the word are muddled

explanation.surface: Muddled brides throw things away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish or scattered remains, waste material.

clue.text: Make provision for books put aside

definitions.meaning: to fit a room with ledges for storing books
to postpone or set a plan aside

explanation.surface: Someone sets up storage for books and then abandons the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting bookcases and deferring a plan are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Score six to open in a forceful way

indicators.note: to open puts the number at the start of the score word

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a tally is a running score

explanation.surface: A batsman hits a six to open the scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests twenty or cricket runs, but here it means a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with vigour and energy, in a lively, powerful manner.

clue.text: Old stager Tree, perhaps, in the lead

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for lead

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army or procession

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Herbert Beerbohm Tree, a veteran actor, perhaps playing the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' suggests the actor Herbert Beerbohm Tree; 'perhaps' turns TREE into ETER, which 'in' places inside VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced old hand who has been around a long time.

clue.text: End call with difficulty, say

definitions.meaning: to replace the telephone receiver to end a conversation
an emotional problem or inhibition, an example of a difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone ends a phone call with difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the phone down ends a call, and a neurosis is a psychological hitch.

clue.text: Sound system for identifying sailors' dives

definitions.text: Sound system for identifying sailors' dives

parts.words: Sound system for identifying sailors' dives
parts.note: a naval echo-sounding device that detects submerged submarines, not a hi-fi or a set of seedy bars

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker system for spotting sailors' seedy bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dives' looks like seedy bars, but means submarines diving, detected by early British sonar.
explanation.definitionFit: The early British name for sonar, which detects submarines by echoes.

clue.text: Bill crazy about redhead

indicators.note: about means the word for crazy goes around the head letter

parts.note: daft means silly or crazy
the head of red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A man called Bill is crazy about a redheaded woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a banking document; 'redhead' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker's draft is an order for payment, a kind of bill of exchange.

clue.text: Base habit less messy

indicators.note: messy suggests these letters are put in a muddled new order

explanation.surface: Messy habits make a person seem lowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like an adjective meaning low, but is the verb, to found.
explanation.definitionFit: To base something is to found or set it up on firm ground.

clue.text: General stall

definitions.meaning: General William ... founded the Salvation Army
a small ...-like enclosure for selling goods or voting

explanation.surface: A military general's market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army founder's surname is also a kiosk or cubicle.

clue.text: Stick in the saloon -it will make a change

definitions.text: Stick in the saloon -it will make a change

parts.words: Stick in the saloon -it will make a change
parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, and the stick in it changes gears

explanation.surface: Someone tries staying in the pub bar for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' looks like a bar, but is the British name for a sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: The lever used to select gears in a car.

clue.text: Some co-operation works

indicators.note: some of the word means a run of its letters is taken from inside it

explanation.surface: Some cooperation makes things work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' is a plural noun, artistic works, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is the plural of opus, so it means works.

clue.text: One of the miners short-handed, say?

definitions.meaning: a coal miner who works down a pit
Isaac ... invented a famous system of shorthand

explanation.surface: A miner is short-handed down the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit worker is a collier, and Pitman's system is shorthand writing.

clue.text: Town so poorly equipped produces single entry

definitions.meaning: a small backward town is called this, as if it had only one steed
a stable that enters just one runner in a race

explanation.surface: A town so badly off that it produces a single entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A backward little place is so called, and a race with one runner fits too.
